short_summary: Mark Thompson announced he will remain chief executive of CNN after the Paramount Skydance acquisition closes.

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.title: Mark Thompson will remain chief executive at CNN after Paramount sale

paragraphs: Mark Thompson will continue to serve as chair and chief executive of CNN after the upcoming corporate sale. He shared this update in a memo sent to network staff on Monday morning. The transaction involves Paramount Skydance taking control of CNN after merging with its parent company, Warner Bros Discovery. The formal closing of the deal is expected on Tuesday.

David Ellison, the chief executive of Paramount Skydance, will lead the newly combined company. According to Thompson, the new leadership values news alongside entertainment and supports the tradition of independent journalism at CNN. Because of these discussions, Thompson will lead the network into its next chapter as an independent editor-in-chief.

This decision brought relief to many CNN employees who worried about a complete overhaul of the organization. Some staff members had previously feared that Ellison might replace leadership with Bari Weiss, who will actually remain in her position as editor in chief of CBS News. CNN employees expressed relief at hearing the news about Thompson, who joined the network in 2023 after previous leadership roles at the BBC and the New York Times.

While the two networks share a parent company, it remains unclear how CNN and CBS News will integrate, given their different structures and audiences. Paramount also agreed to establish a five-person news editorial independence board within 180 days as part of a legal settlement with state attorneys general. Thompson acknowledged that employees felt some uncertainty about the future, but he expressed optimism about working with the new team.

facts.fact: Mark Thompson will remain chief executive and editor-in-chief at CNN after Paramount Skydance takes control of the company following a merger with Warner Bros Discovery.
David Ellison will lead the combined company, and the deal is expected to close on Tuesday.
Paramount agreed to create a five-person news editorial independence board within 180 days as part of a settlement with state attorneys general.
Bari Weiss will remain in her role as editor in chief of CBS News.
